items.title: Banana fritter trader arrested for threatening man with knife in Cheras
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 38-year-old man was arrested for threatening a trader with a knife during a disagreement over roadside business activities in Bandar Tasik Selatan, Cheras, this afternoon. Cheras police chief assistant commissioner Rosdi Daud said the incident occurred in front of Residensi Sateri, Jalan Tasik Selatan 21, a round 3pm, when a man was allegedly slapped and threatened with a knife. He said the suspect was detained at a nearby banana fritter stall to assist in the investigation, and police also seized the knife believed to have been used in the incident.

items.title: Hackers steal US$112mil from French bank
items.summary: PARIS: French lender Credit Mutuel Arkea said on Thursday hackers had stolen around €100 million (US$112.61 million) in a cyber heist and it was working to try to recover the money, in a rare case of cybercriminals successfully stealing from a mainstream bank. French prosecutors said they were investigating the heist. The attackers used an account belonging to Credit Mutuel Arkea to carry out "fraudulent transactions", Credit Mutuel Arkea said in a statement on Wednesday.

items.title: Johari: Lynas-US cooperation to facilitate rare earth supply agreement
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Cooperation between Lynas Rare Earths Ltd (Australia) and the United States government aims to facilitate a material supply agreement for the advanced manufacturing industry. Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said this would support US efforts to achieve its national supply chain resilience objectives. "Within the complex value chain of the rare earth elements (REE) industry, Lynas Malaysia's operations are at the initial processing stage, involving the separation of raw REE mined in Australia into rare earth oxide (REO) supplies.

items.title: Anis Rizana, Armed Forces chief among 218 Perak honours recipients
items.summary: Anis Rizana, a former director-general of the Customs Department, will receive the Darjah Seri Paduka Mahkota Perak, which carries the title Datuk Seri. Armed Forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman will receive the Darjah Datuk Seri Panglima Taming Sari, also carrying the title Datuk Seri, while Accountant-General Nasran Omar will receive the Darjah Datuk Paduka Cura Si Manja Kini, which carries the title Datuk. The other awards comprise the Darjah Ahli Paduka Cura Si Manja Kini for 10 recipients, Darjah Ahli Paduka Mahkota Perak for 28, Darjah Ahli Cura Si Manja Kini (ACM) for 18, and Darjah Ahli Mahkota Perak for 47.

items.title: France workers strike, march for 'dignified wage'
items.summary: PARIS: Thousands of striking workers protested across France on Thursday against the rising cost of living in a new escalation following weeks of demonstrations, with police firing tear gas as violence and vandalism broke out in some cities. More than 270,000 people had already taken to the streets across the country, the interior ministry reported, before a major march kicked off in Paris from 2pm (1300 GMT). The unions are calling for across-the-board wage raises, tax reforms and better learning conditions for young people and have complained about police restrictions on certain protests.

items.title: KKDW reallocates RM200mil from rural housing to settle road project arrears
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Constraints in implementing the Sejahtera People's Housing Programme (PPRS) have prompted the Rural and Regional Development Ministry to reallocate RM200 million from its 2026 allocation to settle outstanding payments for rural road projects. Deputy Minister Datuk Rubiah Wang said the constraints included land ownership disputes among heirs, a lack of suitable sites and overlapping applicants' names. "That means we can issue a NOC for rural road projects.

items.title: No notice yet on special or regular Negri Sembilan assembly sitting — assemblyman
items.summary: "However, I believe it is important for the state assembly to convene to table the state budget, as it is closely linked to the people's interests," he said when met at a Deepavali aid event in Kuala Klawang. Danni said the state budget would determine the state's future, and all parties should make the right decisions in the best interests of Negri Sembilan residents. "Everyone, including the people of the state, hopes the state budget can be tabled.

items.title: Three more tankers damaged in Hormuz as Iran steps up pressure on Trump
items.summary: DUBAI: Iran reported three more tankers had been damaged in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, making clear that shipping would remain in peril as long as the war in the Gulf is unresolved, now that US voters have punished President Donald Trump for waging it. In a mocking reply on Thursday, Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, Vance's opposite number at previous peace talks, accused Vance of letting Trump double down like a "losing gambler" by planning more US strikes. If Vance believed the war was a mistake he should persuade Trump to call it off, Qalibaf said: "Skip the TED talk.

items.title: Shah Alam at risk of major floods without alternative waterways, says Khir Toyo
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Shah Alam remains at risk of major flooding unless alternative waterways are built to divert excess rainwater from existing rivers, says former Selangor menteri besar Dr Mohamad Khir Toyo He said the risk was likely to increase due to rapid development in surrounding areas and Shah Alam's lower elevation compared with neighbouring areas. Khir Toyo said Shah Alam was situated in a low-lying valley compared with surrounding areas such as Sungai Buloh, Rawang and Petaling Jaya. "This causes water to accumulate and stagnate in low-lying areas such as Shah Alam," he said.

items.title: Melaka election: Choose candidates who have 'direct line' to PM's Office, says Anwar
items.summary: MELAKA: Voters in the Melaka election should choose elected representatives who have a "direct line" to the Prime Minister's Office to ensure smooth development processes and the protection of residents' welfare. Pakatan Harapan chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said good relations and alignment of direction between the federal administration and assemblymen were vital to ensuring the smooth implementation of development projects and public welfare policies. Citing the PH candidates for the Paya Rumput and Kelebang seats as examples, Anwar said both candidates share the same direction as the federal government, and their credibility and integrity are greatly needed to effectively translate government policies at the grassroots level.

items.title: Bomb hoaxes hit 27 flights across Europe, trigger fighter jet escorts
items.summary: ROME: Hoax bomb threats hit at least 27 affected flights around Europe on Thursday from Ireland to Bulgaria, the second wave this week, forcing some to make unplanned landings and prompting fighter jets to escort or intercept others. Eric Schouten, head of the aviation security group Dyami, said most of the countries affected supported Ukraine in its war against Russia's invasion. Bulgaria's air force said its fighter jets had escorted three airliners to the ground.

items.title: Traffic smooth on major highways as of 10pm
items.summary: "For northbound traffic along the North-South Expressway, congestion was reported over a 4km stretch between Sungkai and Slim River, as well as along a one-kilometre stretch at the Menora Tunnel heading towards Kuala Kangsar, due to accidents. "Congestion was also reported at Juru heading towards Perai and on the Penang Bridge heading towards Perai," the spokesman told Bernama when contacted. For southbound traffic, congestion was detected at Sedenak heading towards Kulai, while traffic along the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Expressway and East Coast Expressway 1 (LPT1) remained smooth.

items.title: Trump's Iran war gamble backfires as voters weaken his grip on power
items.summary: Trump went to war seeking regime change in Iran. Across the Gulf, officials were left wondering which way Trump would turn. A full-scale assault on Iran now looks less likely, they said.

items.title: US election puts decades of bipartisan support for Israel under strain
items.summary: Many winning candidates were progressives who campaigned against military aid to Israel and the US-Israeli war on Iran. Israel's campaign in Gaza and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's embrace of President Donald Trump and other Republicans had already strained decades of bipartisan support for Israel. There were also signs that Republicans might reexamine their party's traditional support for Israel.

items.title: Five-day high tide phenomenon expected in Klang from Saturday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Klang residents have been asked to remain vigilant as a five-day high tide phenomenon is expected to begin this Saturday, with sea levels at Port Klang forecast to reach 5.2 metres. Under the Port Klang water-level indicators, readings of between 5.0 and 5.3 metres are classified as warning level, while readings of 5.4 to 5.5 metres are considered dangerous The sea level is forecast to reach 5.1 metres at 4.23am on Saturday before rising to 5.2 metres at 5.02am on Sunday. Afternoon high tides are forecast to range between 4.0 and 4.8 metres throughout the period, with peak readings expected between 4.53pm on Saturday and 7.02pm on Wednesday.

items.title: Grab to cut driver fees, cap deductions at 32pct in Vietnam
items.summary: HANOI: Vietnam's competition commission said on Thursday that ride-hailing firm Grab had agreed to cut some fees charged to passengers and drivers and compensate drivers affected by excessive deductions. The announcement follows the government watchdog's preliminary review of complaints from drivers between late August and mid-September about declining fares, commissions and other deductions that they said were hurting earnings. Grab proposed six measures, including a small reduction in app usage fees charged to drivers and capping the combined fees it collects at no more than 32 per cent of the total amount paid by passengers.

items.title: NST Leader: Malaysia's digital ambitions must not outpace cyber defences
items.summary: Malaysia faces the threat of cyberattacks, warned Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. It is inevitable, driven by Malaysia's 30-year advancement to become Southeast Asia's digital powerhouse. In this decade, the Malaysia Digital Economy Blueprint produced hyper growth, a high-income digital economy and accelerated 5G mobilisation.

items.title: Parliamentary inquiry considered over Indonesian Vice-President Gibran's education credentials
items.summary: Neither Jokowi nor Gibran has a party represented in parliament. Three parties within Prabowo's camp and one outside the coalition said they were currently considering three legislative courses of action, officials said. Another party within Prabowo's camp, the National Awakening Party, is "seriously" considering the three options, said party official Muhammad Khozin in a statement.

items.title: Six dead, several injured in New York house fire
items.summary: NEW YORK: Six people died in a house fire early Thursday in New York, authorities said, with Mayor Zohran Mamdani describing the blaze at a Brooklyn home as "devastating." "I am heartbroken to announce that six New Yorkers lost their lives," Mamdani told reporters, noting that firefighters had responded in under four minutes. "Four were dead upon FDNY's arrival, while two more passed away at the hospital.," Mamdani added, referring to the city's fire department.

items.title: Anwar: Leaders should put younger generation ahead of personal interests
items.summary: MELAKA: Political leaders must prioritise the future of the younger generation over personal wealth and interests, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said the country's future depended on leaders committed to safeguarding public funds and ensuring children from all communities had access to better opportunities. Anwar said political leaders should look beyond their personal interests and consider the kind of country they would leave behind for future generations.

items.title: #NSTviral: Strong winds send trader's stall rolling across road in Sepang
items.summary: "Be strong, all you traders," the user wrote. The video showed the stall being swept along the road by strong winds during a heavy downpour. Another Threads user, @fasihahhaziz, said strong winds had battered the area.

items.title: Thailand fossil teeth reveal prehistoric 'giant rat' weighing 30kg
items.summary: BANGKOK: A giant rodent weighing around 30 kilogrammes roamed what is now southern Thailand 33 to 35 million years ago, scientists said, after identifying a previously unknown species from two fossilised teeth. The ancient animal, which one geologist on the team called a "giant rat", was among the largest known from the Paleogene period, offering new clues about how early rodents evolved to enormous sizes. Pannipa Tian, a geologist with Thailand's Department of Mineral Resources who found the incisor, said she initially misidentified the fossil because of its "unusually large size."

items.title: Melaka eyes exporting Kampung Digital model across Asean [WATCH]
items.summary: MELAKA: The Melaka government intends to market its 'Kampung Digital' (Digital Village) model across the Asean region once the rural digitalisation initiative has been fully streamlined and upgraded. Caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the model holds strong potential to be introduced to neighbouring countries as an innovative framework for residential address management and public service delivery. Ab Rauf said 'Kampung Digital' was conceived to overcome structural flaws in traditional rural addressing, where hundreds of residents often shared a single generic postal address, complicating postal deliveries and emergency responses.

items.title: Thailand bans textbook on national security grounds over monarchy content
items.summary: BANGKOK: Thailand has banned a textbook about the country on national security grounds, with the tome's exiled editor saying Thursday it was outlawed over its content on the Thai monarchy. The book's first edition, released in 2019, was not banned, Pavin told AFP. - BAN 'DOESN'T WORK' - In a Facebook post, Pavin said the order helped promote the book.

items.title: 'Resolving Melaka's flood woes remains one of my aspirations' —Ab Rauf [WATCH]
items.summary: MELAKA: Tackling flood issues in Melaka remains a foremost priority for Caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, particularly in addressing deficiencies within the drainage network and mitigating the impact of rising water levels on residential settlements. He said the state administration has initiated several measures alongside relevant agencies to enhance water drainage systems, including securing Federal Government funding for flood mitigation schemes. It remains my top priority to resolve Melaka's flood problems," he said.

items.title: Melaka polls: Bersatu candidate demands public apology over old viral video
items.summary: MELAKA: A Bersatu candidate in the state election has given those responsible for circulating a video linking him to an altercation with a local authority officer 24 hours to issue a public apology and clear his name, failing which he will take legal action. Datuk Norhizam Hassan Baktee, who is contesting the Pengkalan Batu seat, said the video, which went viral on Threads, was an old recording, although he could not recall the exact date of the incident. "The video is very old.

items.title: BN-PN understanding at a good level, says Ab Rauf [WATCH]
items.summary: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) will unveil a joint manifesto for the first time today in conjunction with the 16th Melaka State Election, aiming to secure more than 21 of the 28 State Legislative Assembly seats. Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the manifesto would serve as a comprehensive pledge offering substantial benefits to the people of the state. He said this during a recording session of the Podcast Utama Edisi Khas Buletin TV3 for the 16th Melaka State Election.

items.title: Loke: Defeating BN-PN in Melaka polls no easy feat
items.summary: MELAKA: Overcoming Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional will be no easy feat, particularly as political rivals seek to consolidate their strength amid multi-cornered contests. DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said he hoped voters in Melaka would consolidate their ballots behind PH to avoid split votes that could inadvertently hand victory to their rivals. "Defeating BN and Perikatan Nasional is not easy.

items.title: Melaka plans to amend enactment, register livestock using QR codes [WATCH]
items.summary: MELAKA: The Melaka government plans to amend relevant state enactments to enable livestock to be registered using Quick Response (QR) codes next year, facilitating the tracing of owners in the event of road accidents or cattle theft. Caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the move is an extension of the state's digitalisation drive previously introduced under the 'Kampung Digital' programme. He said the system would allow an owner's details to be retrieved by scanning the QR code, particularly when stray livestock cause traffic collisions.

items.title: A-GC seeking review of decision to free Da'i Syed of rape charge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) will file an application for a review of the Court of Appeal's decision to acquit and discharge celebrity preacher Da'i Syed of a rape charge. Yesterday, Da'i Syed, whose real name is Syed Shah Iqmal Syed Mohd Shaiful, was acquitted and discharged by the Court of Appeal of a rape charge involving a woman seven years ago. The decision was reached by a 2-1 majority, with judges Datuk Azman Abdullah, who chaired the panel, and Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid allowing Syed Shah Iqmal's appeal.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms, heavy rain in eight states and Labuan tonight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit several areas in eight states and Labuan till 10pm tonight. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said that the affected areas include Kubang Pasu, Baling, Sik and Padang Terap in Kedah; Lipis, Raub, Cameron Highlands and Rompin in Pahang, along with Larut Matang, Kampar, Kinta, Kuala Kangsar, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Hulu Perak, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Muallim, Batang Padang and Selama in Perak. Other areas include Gua Musang in Kelantan, Hulu Selangor, Kuala Selangor, Gombak, Sabak Bernam and Klang in Selangor, as well as Kota Tinggi, Johor Bahru and Mersing in Johor.

items.title: Election of first Muslim to US Senate is lesson against racial politics, says Anwar
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 5 — The historic election of the first Muslim to the United States Senate should serve as a lesson for all on the importance of rejecting racial prejudice and religious discrimination, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He cited Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s victory in Michigan as an example of how political participation could transcend racial and religious differences. Anwar said the victory demonstrated how rejecting racial prejudice could become a powerful message for political change.

items.title: Zahid urges ‘respect’ between BN, Perikatan as Melaka campaigning intensifies
items.summary: ISTANBUL, Nov 5 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has reminded all party machinery to exercise restraint and conduct their campaigning responsibly during the 16th Melaka State Election. Ahmad Zahid said excessive campaigning, including raising issues unrelated to the state election, would not change the stance or decisions already made by voters. For the latest news on the Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/.

items.title: Flash floods hit Sungai Buloh, Puncak Alam after heavy rain (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Several areas around Puncak Alam, Selangor, were hit by flash floods this afternoon following prolonged heavy rain, leaving several roads inundated. According to Harian Metro , other affected areas included Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Puncak Alam, Alam Suria and Jalan Meru near the Kampung Bukit Cerakah junction. Heavy rain reportedly continued in Puncak Alam until around 5pm.

items.title: Tengku Puteri Zainah, former wife of Najib, dies at 70
items.summary: KUANTAN, Nov 5 — Tengku Puteri Zainah Tengku Eskandar, the mother of Pahang Investment, Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation Committee chairman Datuk Mohamad Nizar Najib, died today. “It is with deep sorrow that I announce the passing of my beloved mother, Tengku Puteri Zainah,” the post read. The eldest son of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak also expressed his appreciation for his mother’s love, sacrifices, and prayers.

items.title: PM Anwar: No reason to keep CSA secret, Cabinet to discuss disclosure tomorrow
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 5 — The government has no objection to disclosing the contents of the Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) signed between the Unity Government, Bersatu and independent Members of Parliament, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said there was no reason to keep the agreement confidential and that he would raise the matter with Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, who oversees the arrangement, at tomorrow’s Cabinet meeting for further action. Anwar was responding to PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan’s call for the government to disclose the contents of the agreement.

items.title: Nilai teen tests positive for three drugs after dazed vaping video prompts police investigation
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 5 — A male secondary school student in Nilai has tested positive in a preliminary urine screening for three types of drugs, namely ketamine, benzodiazepines and THC. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the 17-year-old student was being investigated following the circulation of a video on social media showing him allegedly in a dazed state after vaping. Alzafny said the video was believed to have been circulated on October 28 at a secondary school in the district.

items.title: Sarawak eyes 2050 plan to spread jobs, services and growth beyond major cities
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Nov 5 — Sarawak is considering a long-term urban development policy through 2050 to guide settlement planning and ensure balanced development across major cities, smaller towns and rural areas. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said the proposed Sarawak Urban Development Policy 2050 would provide long-term direction for the state's urban and settlement system, taking into account its vast geographical landscape and diverse communities. Abang Johari said development planning should also take into account the different needs of smaller towns, riverine settlements, rural communities and interior areas.

items.title: RM1.5m facelift for Penang Assembly includes heritage gallery, lactation room and upgraded media area
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 5 — The Penang State Legislative Assembly has implemented several infrastructure improvements and upgrading works at its building here, involving a cost of RM1.5 million. This was undertaken in conjunction with the Second Meeting of the Fourth Session of the 15th Penang State Legislative Assembly. Law said the special media conference area had also been upgraded to provide greater comfort for media practitioners covering the assembly sitting.

items.title: Batu Caves ritual video: Youth repents publicly with family at Shah Alam mosque
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 5 — A 21-year-old Muslim youth whose participation in Hindu rituals at a Batu Caves temple sparked a controversy made a public declaration of repentance today alongside his mother and younger sister, prior to undergoing court-ordered faith rehabilitation. Reciting the Islamic declaration of faith before state religious officials at the Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Mosque here, Aliff Daniel Adli renounced the Hindu and Buddhist rituals he had previously engaged in, acknowledging that his actions violated Islamic tenets and caused widespread distress. His mother, Rohizayanti Ramli, and younger sister, Nur Ranea Ezreen Adli, made their own formal declarations of repentance, expressing regret over failing to guide and counsel him away from external influences that conflicted with Islamic teachings.

items.title: Ramanan: Mitra allocates RM755,390 to upgrade facilities at 21 Tamil schools in Melaka
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 5 — The Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra) has allocated RM755,390 to 21 Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Tamil (SJKT) in Melaka this year to enhance teaching and learning facilities. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the allocation covered various initiatives, including MADANI furniture assistance, tuition classes and digital learning tools such as smartboards. Ramanan said SJKT Jasin Lalang had received RM47,560 under the initiatives.

items.title: No transfer letter received, Shuhaily remains border agency chief, lawyer says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Embattled Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MBCA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain has yet to receive an official transfer letter from the Home Ministry, leaving him legally empowered to lead the agency despite ministerial statements that he is being returned to the police force. Rafique called on Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail to address the administrative ambiguity, arguing that public pronouncements of an impending transfer had generated confusion and invited unnecessary speculation. The clarification follows Saifuddin's announcement last week that the Home Ministry had decided to terminate Shuhaily's secondment to MBCA and return him to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).

items.title: Govt expands Sabah sea surveillance system to plug maritime monitoring gaps
items.summary: Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said the project was approved under the First Rolling Plan of the 13th Malaysia Plan for 2026 to address gaps in maritime surveillance coverage across Malaysian waters, with the tender process expected to begin by year-end. “All 15 MMEA RSS stations operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, providing continuous surveillance within their respective coverage areas,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today. However, Shamsul Anuar said the radar stations’ continuous operation did not provide complete surveillance coverage of Malaysian waters, with MMEA deploying ships and boats to patrol areas beyond the system’s coverage.

items.title: Liew Chin Tong urges accountants to embrace multidisciplinary skills as AI reshapes finance profession
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong has urged accountants and finance professionals to be multidisciplinary as the positive and negative impacts of artificial intelligence (AI) emerge and continue to occupy the minds of finance leaders in the years ahead. He said AI would displace some less sophisticated jobs held by accountants but would probably create new ones requiring deeper human judgement, fewer technical skills and more value-based decision-making. ASEAN states would need to create a sizable middle class rich enough to consume the outputs from the productive capacity in the region,” he said.

items.title: No water found in RON95 so far, but Petron and Caltex are offering goodwill payment to motorists with damaged engines
items.summary: Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the compensation measures were initiated on a goodwill basis for verified complaints while investigations into the incidents continued. On the investigation, Armizan said preliminary analysis of 43 petrol samples by the Chemistry Department had found no evidence of water contamination. Armizan said 262 RON95 petrol samples had been collected from eight states and three oil company depots since complaints first emerged on Oct 3.

items.title: Two Thai nationals face death penalty for allegedly killing MMEA officer in Sungai Padang
items.summary: KANGAR, Nov 5 — Two Thai nationals were charged at the Magistrate’s Court here today with the murder of a Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) officer late last month. Both accused were jointly charged with the murder of Mohd Roshaimi Mohd Ridzuan, 41, near the Malaysian Fisheries Development Authority jetty in Sungai Padang here between 11 pm on Oct 26 and 1.30 am on Oct 27. The charge was framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same Code, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years and not less than 12 strokes of the cane if not sentenced to death, upon conviction.

items.title: Takiyuddin: CSA funding terms must be made public like 2021 MoU
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) chief whip Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan today demanded full transparency over the recent Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) signed by 13 Opposition MPs, questioning the delay in terms disclosure, implementation details, and allocation figures. Speaking at a press conference in Parliament, the Kota Bharu MP drew a contrast between the current pact signed on October 31 and the historic 2021 bipartisan Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed under the Ismail administration, which explicitly guaranteed public disclosure and equal constituency funding. He stressed that under the 2021 agreement, all Opposition MPs involved were allocated funding equivalent to government lawmakers.

items.title: Driving home for Deepavali? 3.28 million vehicles expected daily on PLUS and major highways
items.summary: Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) director-general Ir Mohd Hadzmir Yusoff said traffic volume is expected to increase from today as motorists head towards the East Coast and the northern and southern parts of the country. He said the PLUS highway network is projected to record 2.24 million vehicles, followed by the Duta-Ulu Kelang Expressway (DUKE) with 288,000 and the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Expressway (KLK) with 190,000. “The East Coast Expressway Phase 1 (LPT1) is projected to record 83,000 vehicles, while the East Coast Expressway Phase 2 (LPT2) is expected to see 44,000 vehicles,” he said in a statement here today.

items.title: Malaysia’s daily afternoon downpour returns with a 10-state thunderstorm warning
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has again issued an afternoon thunderstorm advisory for multiple states across the country, forecasting heavy downpours, lightning, and gusty winds until 4.00pm today. In the northern peninsula, stormy weather is expected across five Kedah districts: Baling, Sik, Kulim, Bandar Baharu, and Kuala Muda. The warning concurrently extends across mainland Penang through Seberang Perai Utara, Seberang Perai Tengah, and Seberang Perai Selatan, while Perak faces widespread disruption across nine districts, namely Kerian, Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Larut Matang, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, and Muallim.

items.title: Daiso’s largest global distribution centre on Pulau Indah a vote of confidence in Malaysia, says Anwar
items.summary: PORT KLANG, Nov 5 — The decision by Japanese retail giant Daiso to establish its largest global distribution centre (GDC) on Pulau Indah, Selangor, reflects international confidence in Malaysia’s economic stability, infrastructure and long-term potential, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. He said such investments reflected Malaysia’s ability to leverage its strategic location, established port infrastructure and skilled workforce to attract companies looking to strengthen their global supply chains. “So when a company like Daiso chooses Pulau Indah here for its largest GDC worldwide, it must certainly convey a profound message about the company and about this country.

items.title: Zahid: 2,364 tahfiz students take up skills training, 900 secure Malaysian Skills Certification
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — A total of 2,364 tahfiz students enrolled in various skills training programmes at Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions between 2023 and 2025, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. Ahmad Zahid, who is also the National TVET Council (MTVET) chairman, said data from the Department of Skills Development (JPK) under the Human Resources Ministry (Kesuma) also showed that 900 tahfiz students had obtained Malaysian Skills Certification under the National Occupational Skills Standard (NOSS). In a written reply to Datuk Ahmad Saad @ Yahya (PN-Pokok Sena) posted on the Parliament website on the progress and challenges in implementing tahfiz TVET programmes, Ahmad Zahid said the NOSS certification comprised 609 students at Level 3, 285 at Level 4 and six at Level 5.

items.title: Govt open to stronger support framework for SMEs moving beyond initial growth, says Fadillah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The government welcomes the business community’s proposal for more structured support for growth-stage small and medium enterprises (SMEs), said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof. Fadillah said equal attention must be given to helping businesses sustain their growth after achieving initial success. On artificial intelligence (AI), Fadillah said technology adoption should be guided by its ability to solve problems and serve people better.

items.title: Oil ‘cocktail’ exports put Malaysia’s palm oil credentials under scrutiny, says maritime industry veteran
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The alleged blending of imported cooking oil with locally produced supplies before it is re-exported under a Malaysian label has raised concerns over product origin, traceability and food safety, with calls for the authorities to investigate the practice. Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said the alleged practice, which industry players have described as an oil “cocktail”, warranted closer scrutiny from the authorities, particularly over product origin, quality and food safety. The Edge reported yesterday, citing industry sources, that imported palm oil was allegedly being blended with local supplies before being re-exported, potentially allowing foreign-origin oil to be marketed as Malaysian palm oil.

items.title: Matrade warns businesses of scammers posing as agency officers to solicit upfront payments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) has alerted the business community and the public to fraudulent activities by individuals impersonating its personnel via email and WhatsApp. Matrade said the perpetrators targeted vendors under the pretext of procuring urgent services for overseas trade delegations, booth translation services for international exhibitions, and corporate recreational events. “Matrade never requires vendors to deposit advances or settle external invoices with third-party sub-contractors,” it said.

items.title: Armizan: Preliminary tests on 43 RON95 samples find no significant water contamination
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Preliminary laboratory tests on 43 petrol samples found water content below the minimum detection level, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. “According to the preliminary report received from the Department of Chemistry dated October 29, 2026, all 43 samples analyzed recorded a water content of less than 0.05 per cent,” he said during Question Time. Perak received 25 complaints involving various petrol stations in the state throughout October.

items.title: Rapid KL train congestion: Anthony Loke vows fix after PM’s directive
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Nov 5 — The Transport Ministry is actively working to resolve train service congestion and overcome technical challenges faced by rail operators, says Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook. We will resolve these technical issues to improve the service,” he said. On Oct 30, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim directed the Transport Minister to swiftly resolve train congestion issues, expressing concern that they disrupt the public’s daily routine.

items.title: Anwar heads to Melaka to drum up Pakatan momentum ahead of Nov 14 polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to attend five programmes in Melaka tomorrow, including participating in Pakatan Harapan (PH) campaign activities in conjunction with the Melaka State Election. Anwar said two of the programmes he would be attending are the 2026 Prime Minister’s Golden Hand Award (MATEPM) ceremony and the Melaka State Madani Aspirations Tour. “Insya-Allah, I will be in Melaka tomorrow for several engagements in this historic state.

items.title: Heading east for Deepavali? Concessionaire releases travel time advisory for KLK and LPT1
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Highway concessionaire AFA Prime Berhad has activated its Travel Time Advisory for the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Highway (KLK) and the East Coast Expressway Phase 1 (LPT1) ahead of an anticipated holiday traffic surge for Deepavali. The staggered travel schedule aims to ease bottlenecks across the arterial eastern corridor, particularly at the high-volume Gombak, Bentong, and Jabor toll plazas that link the Klang Valley to Pahang, Terengganu, and Kelantan. For outbound journeys from Kuala Lumpur and Selangor on Saturday, Nov 7, motorists passing through the Gombak Toll Plaza are advised to stagger their departures according to their destination.

items.title: Seven foreigners held, RM1.08m in drugs seized in Bukit Mertajam raids
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 5 — Police arrested seven foreigners and seized suspected methylenedioxy methamphetamine (MDMA) powder and ketamine worth RM1.08 million during raids on two premises in Bukit Tengah here on Nov 1. Seberang Perai Tengah (SPT) district police chief ACP Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said a team from the district Narcotics Crime Investigation Division raided the premises at 12.50 am following surveillance and intelligence gathering. Nik Aminuddin said urine screening tests revealed that two of the suspects tested positive for methamphetamine, while the other five tested negative.

items.title: Deepavali toll relief: 50pc discount on major highways this Friday and Saturday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Motorists travelling across the country for the Deepavali celebrations will enjoy a 50 per cent toll discount on Friday and Saturday, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi announced today. Putrajaya estimates the two-day toll concession will require approximately RM20.11 million in federal compensation payouts to highway concessionaires, subject to post-holiday traffic volume verifications. The discount applies to private Class 1 passenger vehicles across all interstate expressways, alongside Class 2 commercial vehicles crossing the Penang Bridge.
